1.SubTitle: Eugene's Diary 1
1.Content:
I seriously cannot believe my bad luck today! I've just been manhandled by the most obstinate Celestial I've ever had the misfortune of talking to. Although I suppose I am fortunate he did not seek to kill me, only to declare—very insistently, I might add—that my supposed Hypogean companion has stolen two very important ancient weapons of his, and I am to be the one to show him how to get them back. 
    Ancient weapons? What on earth is he talking about!? I work alone. I would not, and have never, taken on fellow Hypogean into my confidence. But this Celestial is nothing if not stubborn. He will hear naught of what I have to say on the matter. His only wish is to prevent me from escaping until I can somehow give him what he wants. In other words, I'm now under the effects of a peculiar spell and have been kidnapped!
    I swear I, Eugene, have never been so insulted in my life...

2.SubTitle: Eugene's Diary 2
2.Content:
It won't take us long to chase down the offending Hypogean stuck in the Celestial's bad books. Figures. Now comes the delicate matter of how the brain-dead Celestial "Pigeonhead" is going to handle my release. Is he a Celestial of his word?
    So what explains my new favorite moniker for this fool: "Pigeonhead"? Because he lacks manners. Because I keep asking him his name and he keeps refusing to answer. Because I have no choice but to go with the option that most closely resembles his defects?
    Then again, I've always used nicknames for their kind since they all seem to be afflicted with those deformed pigeon wings of theirs.

3.SubTitle: Eugene's Diary 3
3.Content:
When we finally closed in on that Hypogean, ol' Pigeonhead was quite the eager beaver. I was happy to follow a plan. Not him. He bolted after the darned thing and... who do I talk to get a new partner?
    Pigeonhead bit off more than he could chew. My alleged Hypogean partner does have a partner, it seems—many partners, just not me. And so, without further ado, we were on the brink of a cliff and had a very ungraceful descent. One I hadn't had the misfortune of enduring before. The entire trip would've been such a tremendous waste if I hadn't had the foresight to grab that chest of weapons from our enemies' hands at the very last second.

4.SubTitle: Eugene's Diary 4
4.Content:
The dreadful thought has occurred to me that my Pigeonhead companion may not be the great Celestial he claims to be, but a child trafficker! What else am I to do with the fact that the "ancient weapons" are no artifacts at all, but two little demon children still very much in the milk-drinking phase.
    Yet this should not concern me in the slightest. I've already fulfilled my side of the bargain. He got what he wanted. Won't he keep his word and let me go free? Apparently "things are more complicated than I'd realized". What's that supposed to mean? Then he told me a magical device for breaking my curse is broken! In other words, he has a very good reason for keeping me captive a while longer...
    But all of this is academic if I can't find a way out of this demon place. Right, more bad luck. Particularly, the bad luck of jumping out of a frying pan and into a fire or, rather, off a cliff into a network of terrible underground caverns that lead you in circles. And would you believe it? It is in this august place several dragons have decided to make their home!

5.SubTitle: Eugene's Diary 5
5.Content:
It has struck me as distinctly possible that I might have become the very first Hypogean nanny in all of history, which is not a role I have exactly trained for. One of the little naughty brats has a habit of pulling my hair, finding it amusing beyond what any sane creature would think. I keep asking myself: who exactly is the real Hypogean here?
    The baby boy is quite the obedient one, all full of smiles for me. So wonderfully ignorant of the world... Although I have to give him some credit: he is adorable.
    In his infinite wisdom, Pigeonhead the Celestial has decided to put me in charge of the two little brats just in case they ran into some kind of danger. Where I'm from our young are not used to being cuddled in this way. They can't be that delicate?!
    Although normally rather quiet Pigeonhead becomes quite animated whenever I bring up this issue of letting the young'uns exert a greater degree of freedom. I don't have the patience to endure his long spiels.
    No, I need to get away from this madman!

6.SubTitle: Eugene's Diary 6
6.Content:
We lifted the curse! Well done to us, me in particular. Now I can say goodbye to Pigeonhead and his ankle-biters. A few more days of having my hair pulled out by that energetic demon child and I'm going to have to embrace baldness—not the style I was hoping for at this particular moment in my life.
    Gavus even had the temerity to thank me. I don't know what the world is coming to when a Celestial feels himself greatly indebted to a Hypogean? Amazing one of heaven's ugly faces can say that.
    By the way, I finally did figure out Pigeonhead's real name: Gavus. This, of course, he revealed as I was about to walk out of their lives forever. I think I'll stick to Pigeonhead. Of course, that also implies I will never meet him again, which is not likely if I have anything to say about it.

7.SubTitle: Eugene's Diary 7
7.Content:
I've had a few days now to appreciate my glorious freedom, yet my thoughts keep turning back to the fate of Gavus and the little devils.
    It's strange not to be kept up until late at night by screeching... It almost feels as if the wee hours of the morning are missing something? I wonder if the little girl is still trying to destroy her surroundings? Or have the experiences of the last few days mellowed her? It also concerns me that Gavus, while not completely incompetent, may not be up to the challenge of caring for children. Let's just say that any mother that left them to his care would be something less than responsible.
    Darnit! I'm a Hypogean! I need to be thinking Hypogean thoughts! What are these filthy... pangs of conscience?
    But would it be so bad to... visit them after all this time? If only for a few minutes. I shall leave now. There's no harm in it...

8.SubTitle: Eugene's Diary 8
8.Content:
I turned up a little late. My Hypogean cousins do not share my ambivalence toward Pigeonhead and his cursed kids. I arrive to discover he and the children were attacked moments prior, the little ones badly injured.
    Pigeonhead was trying to channel his energies into a healing salve, an endeavor in which I assisted. I can't say it was very effective, but their condition will not worsen for the time being. I feel the experience has wounded Pigeonhead emotionally too. His face has sunk into solid worry as he keeps trying, again and again, to use what little magic he has left to heal the children fully.
    Then when I see Pigeonhead almost fully drain himself of all magicks in his futile quest to heal the children, he turns to me and says: "There may be another way."

9.SubTitle: Eugene's Diary 9
9.Content:
Pigeonhead is mad. He keeps talking to me about finding some "Cradle of Truth" which will allow him to call on his fellow Celestials and then, presumably, all will be well for the children. 
    The little girl spent some time awake today to play with my hair for a few minutes before returning to her deep slumber. The difference is quite noticeable. She is wasting away, her strength fading. I took her hand in mine to help her pull...
    The little ones are vulnerable. I can see Pigeonhead was not exaggerating.
    I suspect Pigeonhead is overextending himself in his healing. Magical exhaustion is not a pleasant prospect. He wouldn't be able to carry on...

10.SubTitle: Eugene's Diary 10
10.Content:
We finally made it out of that hellhole. And when dawn comes Pigeonhead has claimed his fellow Celestials will meet us here, and then the safety of the two young'uns will be assured.
    I think Pigeonhead is grasping at straws. What makes him think his kind will heal two naughty babies? He may have his agenda, but something tells me the Celestials are more inclined to strike first and ask questions later. He's so naive. And won't hear a word of it.
    We're only hours from when my misgivings will be confirmed or denied, and Pigeonhead may be forced to choose between his conscience and the people. I have no desire to fight another battle.
    I hope I'm very much mistaken...

1.SubTitle: Metallurgist Nikolai's Diary 1
1.Content:
Today is the day of our great Guardian, Gaius, declared war on the Celestials!
    What a moment for the ages: when mankind finally turned away from the Heavens to stand upon our own two feet and declare ourselves the masters of our fate!
    What more does mankind need to prove that we are more than equal to the Celestials? Our buildings already tower into the skies and compare with the highest peaks. Skyscraping airships brush against the upper atmosphere and the shoulders of the Celestials' Palaces already.
    Our civilization, its embrace of magical strength, has reached a pinnacle from which mankind can work the greatest miracles! The Celestials should be the ones kneeling to us, not us to them.
    Dearest and most venerable Guardian, I salute you as humanity's envoy and representative of our combined glory and honor. I pledge myself to your service as I should—and everyone ought!
    I've heard the Dean is currently selecting students from the Academy for a personal audience with our mighty leader. As a faithful devotee of your way and your mighty works, I look forward to the incredible day when I can lay eyes on you, your lowliest servant. I look forward to the day I can contribute my blood, sweat, and tears to your cause—sword of your strength, shield of your valor, ready to lay waste to the mountains of the gods!

2.SubTitle: Metallurgist Nikolai's Diary 2
2.Content:
The Dean just took me for an audience with Guardian!
    I had the privilege to overhear our great Guardian's army is facing some difficulties, and so the decision has been made to reduce the minimum age of enlistment by two years. This has upset some of the conscripts in the southern provinces.
    To the reason for our audience with the mighty Guardian. As Chief Astral Mage in the court, our Dean's opinions carry great weight, and he has been advising on the creation of a powerful new artifact using our mastery over the magical energies of the sun and moon. It is to be the most powerful weapon of all time, capable of crushing continents or breaking the sky into pieces. A weapon, in other words, capable of ending this war. Who but our Dean, the most accomplished of human sorcerers, could be commissioned for this project? I and the other students shall serve as his right-hand researchers. And so we begin its construction!
    My mind races with thoughts of my august future given that, at my age, I've already been in the physical presence of our great Guardian! I realize now that history has selected me to be one of its key contributors. And I do believe and have every confidence that my prodigious abilities in metallurgy and alchemy will help forge this amazing weapon.

3.SubTitle: Metallurgist Nikolai's Diary 3
3.Content:
We've already crafted two prototypes of the weapon our Dean sketched out, one named "Dawn" and the other "Dusk". But live demonstrations revealed a destructive power far less than what our great leader had envisioned.
    As I have said before, this result is not unexpected given our Dean's overly conservative methodology. It can't be deployed at full strength of magical.
    If only my co-contributor had the sense to adopt my plan—combining bio-alchemy with the original design—he would find solutions magic alone cannot. His response? "As long as I'm here, you can forget about polluting my lab with your immoral ideas!" This a foolish reply from tired moralizers with nothing to contribute but old ideas.
    It is the most ridiculous situation imaginable, and yet here I am putting it to paper. Here we have a researcher who knows the way forward, whose ideas might hold the key to the weapon's full potential, who is now to be shut down with questions of ethics?!
    I can already tell what will happen if the research team does not change track soon. So there is no point waiting for the outcome. I've already begun my own secret experiments. Bio-alchemy has been rejected by the mainstream for far too long out of a malformed fear that some great disaster will take place upon tampering with the human spirit. It is a fear not borne by any evidence.
    People fear simply what they do not know. That is natural. But I have seen the results firsthand. It should not be a source of dread, but recognized as an untapped source of blessings! Once those blessings are revealed, I shall be thoroughly vindicated and my critics condemned.

4.SubTitle: Metallurgist Nikolai's Diary 4
4.Content:
Today marks the seventh in what is shaping up to be a long week of experiments which have not, I must sadly write, gone as well as I'd expected. It may be a question of size. I suspect younger subjects may be needed...
    New organic entities require an old organic for fuel. It is a sacrifice, yes, but one eminently necessary for the future of human civilization.
    I'm sensing very strongly that I am on the brink of some amazing discovery sure to cement my name on history's page. I need only persist a little longer. I'll be able to present my innovative results directly to the great Guardian himself!
    My newest test subjects should be arriving any moment. And I haven't a moment to waste!

5.SubTitle: Metallurgist Nikolai's Diary 5
5.Content:
Guardian is getting impatient with the misguided efforts of my Dean, just as I'd expected. He toured the laboratory just a few days ago, loudly noting the weapon's power is far from what's required. It seems he is considering scrapping the entire project.
    What wonderful news!
    The time has come for my doubts about Dean's approach shall be utterly vindicated! My newest experiments have been proceeding extraordinarily well, with the latest attachments to my subjects provoking a robust, heightened Invigorating Essence. Even more positively, the bodies of these hybrids showed no sign of rejecting my implants!
    It is essentially a demonstration of the correctness of my approach: the only weapon that can turn the tide of this war is to be found in bio-alchemy.
    I've arranged an audience with Guardian in just three days. I'm almost giddy with thoughts of the glory and prestige I'm about to win for myself in this brave new field of discovery!

6.SubTitle: Metallurgist Nikolai's Diary 6
6.Content:
I can do nothing if not commemorate this day.
    I demonstrated beyond all reasonable doubt to the Guardian the success and viability of my approach, and untapped promises of bio-alchemy. But my dumb old Dean—had the gall to criticize my every decision in front of Guardian himself! He even had the temerity to call my efforts a "disgusting disgrace" to the Academy and repudiation of every ethical boundary ever instituted! I can't believe someone from our Academy just threatened the leader of our people with resignation!
    Guardian abruptly lifted his sword and cleaved his head from his neck. He then pointed straight at me and declared: "Your turn!"
    It's hard to accurately convey the joy and vindication I felt at that moment. My poor old teacher, if only you had come to your senses earlier. We could have worked together! Instead, you had to doubt Guardian's plans and authority—and even threaten the man himself!
    From this moment on I shall be assuming full control of the project, which I'm very determined to lead into a new and exciting era!

7.SubTitle: Metallurgist Nikolai's Diary 7
7.Content:
We have commenced bio-alchemy trials with plenty of subjects on a real scale, and also taken many steps to integrate it with the original weapons. We're making real progress for the first time in ages. The first bio-alchemic weapons test failed, but this was not unanticipated. In a way, it confirms another hypothesis: only by endowing real intelligence into "Dusk" and "Dawn" shall we be able to wield its full strength and turn this war in our favor!
    I must rectify immediately with the construction of an enormous energy field that should provide an ongoing power supply. I have nicknamed it the "Cradle of Truth", symbolically as the weapons mark our emergence from a cradle of vulnerability to a Celestial plane of strength where we are equal to the gods. It's declaration enough to the world that our power is in no way inferior to the output of the sun!
    Of course, not everything can go as planned in such a grand scheme.
    The old Dean had his supporters. I can't be sure whether they are deliberately trying to undermine the project by offering stupid suggestions, or simply too dumb to realize its potential. Their attitudes bother me, particularly after my new ranking. If they don't want to support me with useful ideas, then at least they can get their hands dirty at the coalface of the industry—the difficult construction of the Cradle of Truth. But I'll make sure that the firing mechanism can only be exercised by my hand alone.
    There is much to anticipate in the coming weeks: humanity's ascendancy into a new era.

8.SubTitle: Metallurgist Nikolai's Diary 8
8.Content:
As I'd very much expected, with some disgruntled former classmates who idolized the old Dean and don't like getting their hands dirty on the Cradle of Truth's construction. Gossiping about my "unclean methods", whatever that means? They're extremely envious of my success and that I had them taken out of their cozy lab. For all I know, they're probably planning to destroy the Cradle in the final moments of its construction.
    Heh! The very thought that this project could have ever succeeded with people of that caliber seems laughable. It's time we took a page out of the Guardian's book when it comes to disobedient researchers...
    I try not to let such trivialities affect my mood. Recent trials to integrate consciousness into the weapons are going well. We just need to stay the course and all of our efforts will be rewarded with a masterpiece.
    The very last thing I can do would be to never disappoint our great Guardian and the hopes of humanity. And the worst thing I can do is to allow some fools to endanger this vitally important project.

9.SubTitle: Metallurgist Nikolai's Diary 9
9.Content:
Experiments, experiments, experiments! I've almost lost track of the number of subjects that have passed through these halls.
    I was quite disturbed when I woke up today to receive a very unfortunate update, an update that will forever sear this day with infamy. I have been told our great Guardian himself perished on the front lines while fighting on behalf of all humanity! A cold chill swept through my bones as I realized just how cruel and capricious the Celestials can be. They must be celebrating.
    I've ordered the news be kept secret from all the others here. Let no one breathe a word of it! It will be better for everyone's resolve if the memory of our Guardian is kept blameless, pure, and alive as an invincible warrior on the field whose singular vision is guaranteed to save humanity. I will not let their minds be troubled. His will still live in us—to recover humanity's place in the cosmos.
    And indeed the completion of the project nears at a rapid pace as we put the finishing touches on the new and improved weapons. It'll be our chance to wipe the smiles off those arrogant Celestials.
    The Celestials shall be cast down into the mud as the true masters and commanders of Esperia, humanity, shall go on to achieve greater and greater heights of glory!

10.SubTitle: Metallurgist Nikolai's Diary 10
10.Content:
Heh! Success! The weapons have been successfully modified into a far more powerful state!
    We've achieved a perfect symbiotic union between experimental subject 637 and Dusk. A similar successful result with Dawn should see the project move well and truly beyond the development phase into a more mature frame.
    It is a magnificent thing we have accomplished at the lab today, a miracle of human ingenuity by which we shall achieve miracles for humanity in this war.
    When I look at the little weapons, they remind me of nothing so much as two poor babies who nonetheless have the potential inside to rise and destroy even the gods. And I'll be right there when they do, bearing witness to a delicious spectacle of Celestials crushed under our feet.
    Heh! What can the pathetic Celestials do to us now? It is our time to dominate the world!

11.SubTitle: Metallurgist Nikolai's Diary 11
11.Content:
A messenger from the front has just delivered more bad news. I've just been told a strike team of Celestials is headed here.
    Someone must have leaked word of the project! I would have thought that for the sake of humanity, people could keep their mouths shut, but no. It is especially troubling when I consider Guardian took great care to execute everyone not working directly inside the facility who knew about its existence. Did someone overhear something who survive to tell the tale? A fish slipped the net? Well done, traitor of humanity. Yet I can guess the Celestials still don't realize the project's true potential. If they did, their entire army would be on their way.
    Unfortunately, this has dramatically cut our preparation time. There are just too many things we need to do to wrap this up. All the threads of this project must now be pursued simultaneously.
    The news has also removed the last shreds of guilt I felt for my disgruntled ex-research colleagues whose lives I had to expend on the more difficult aspects of the project's development. But I should have been more efficient in destroying evidence of our existence.
    I can only rest once the weapon has been connected to a secure power source and activated. More time would have been nice, but time is a luxury and, besides, I'd love to see the expressions on their face when the Celestials get to experience our weapon firsthand.

12.SubTitle: Metallurgist Nikolai's Diary 12
12.Content:
Curses! The Celestial attack came far earlier than I'd anticipated. We lost control of the Cradle of Truth! And this stronghold is also in danger. The energy supply is only half completed, and neither of the weapons could be activated. And there's nothing I can do about it.
    No! This was my life, my blood, my handiwork! I'd rather have everything destroyed than see them walk away with my accomplishment!
    I've hidden in the weapons in a place they'll never find! But I must take additional steps to ensure they never discover exactly what we have been working on. Hah! Because they know as long as rumors of this weapon abound, as long as it might potentially exist, they are still in danger and humanity is always on the brink of a comeback.
    Curse you, Celestials! From the depths of Hades, I do curse thee! Savor your victory. Because your Judgment Day is coming. And when it comes, the glory of humanity shall trample you eternally underfoot!
